chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who marries a woman and she gives birth to his child, then she breastfeeds a bondwoman with her milk: Is it permissible for his child from another woman to marry that bondwoman whom she breastfed? He said: 'No, she is like a sister through breastfeeding because the milk comes from the same father.'

key_terms.فَحْلٍ وَاحِدٍ: One father / single source (referring to the milk source)

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding create a marital prohibition between a child and the nursed person?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify that the prohibition of marriage via breastfeeding (radha') extends to the nursemaid herself, establishing her as a 'sister' to the nursing mother's children. This specific case highlights the principle that the milk originates from a single source (the mother), thereby creating a kinship bond equivalent to blood relation, which renders the bondwoman mahram to the children. This underscores the Shia juristic view that the physical act of nursing creates a permanent marital barrier regardless of the nurse's social status.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4671 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who marries a woman, and she gives birth to his child.
Then she breastfeeds a bondwoman with her milk.
Imam (as) was asked: "Is it permissible for his child from another woman to marry that bondwoman whom she breastfed?"
Imam (as) replied: "No, she is like a sister through breastfeeding because the milk comes from the same father."
